name: Laurel Halo
label: Awe
lede: Laurel Halo went from a freeform radio booth in Ann Arbor to Hyperdub, sang on her debut album, then stopped, scored runways and a documentary, and started a label called Awe. Its first release, the piano record Atlas, landed at No. 26 on Pitchfork's 2023 list.

eras.title: A freeform station in Ann Arbor
eras.text: Laurel Anne Chartow grew up in Ann Arbor playing piano, violin and guitar, with a freeform college station on the dial and Detroit's electronic music next door. Her parents both worked in the auto industry. In 2009 she moved to New York.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection · Flow State: Laurel Halo interview
years.h: Laurel Anne Chartow is born in Ann Arbor
years.p: Wikipedia gives her hometown as Ann Arbor, Michigan, where she learned piano, guitar and violin. Her own website says Detroit.
years.xp:
In a 2011 interview with The Quietus she said she grew up playing piano, violin and guitar, and that her parents both worked in the auto industry for decades before having to move on as it failed.

As a kid she was obsessed with the romantic and impressionist piano composers: Debussy, Ravel, Satie, Rachmaninoff, Shostakovich. Those pianos come back on Atlas in 2023.

years.src: The Quietus: Metal Confection · Flow State: Laurel Halo interview · Wikipedia: Laurel Halo
years.h: She DJs on WCBN and lives in a show house called Arborvitae
years.p: WCBN is the University of Michigan's freeform station. Wikipedia dates her career to 2006.
years.xp:
She told The Quietus WCBN is "one of the few remaining freeform stations in the country" and that "you're meant to play all different styles." The first festival she ever went to was the Detroit Electronic Music Festival, which she described as an ear-opening experience.

Her influences, she told Flow State, include Warp and 4AD records and a lot of local Michigan music, from Detroit techno to electro and minimal.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection
years.h: Halo moves to New York and starts working alone
years.p: A band meant a rehearsal space and everyone's schedules, she told The Quietus. In 2009 she left Michigan and began recording by herself.
years.xp: She told The Quietus she loved the people she'd played with, but "it's nice to have total control of what you're doing."

eras.title: King Felix goes online
eras.text: Halo put a first EP online with her own voice on it, and several labels wrote back. She chose Hippos in Tanks, made a second EP, shared a record with Daniel Lopatin and sent demos to Hyperdub.

years.cap: Halo, October 2010, a month before King Felix
q: I was just excited about working with Hippos In Tanks.
years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection
years.h: Hippos in Tanks releases King Felix, with Halo singing
years.p: The EP came out November 30. She had put it online first, and several labels got in touch.
years.xp: Hippos in Tanks offered both a reissue of King Felix and a deal for a new EP, which is how she ended up on the label. She told The Quietus in 2011 she was happy about it.

years.big: "...to do the exact same thing and hammer that one sound into the ground."
years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The Quietus: Metal Confection
years.h: Halo follows King Felix with Hour Logic and sings less
years.p: Halo's answer to what people expect after a successful record, from her 2011 Quietus interview. Hippos in Tanks released the second EP on June 21.
years.xp:
The full line from The Quietus: "People place a lot of expectation on you, if you make one record that is successful, to do the exact same thing and hammer that one sound into the ground."

Her voice is still on Hour Logic, but further back than on King Felix.

years.h: FRKWYS Vol. 7 puts Halo on a record with Daniel Lopatin
years.p: RVNG Intl.'s FRKWYS series pairs her with [[Oneohtrix Point Never|9cea062d-d476-447f-98b4-e67e14bfd1e4]]'s Lopatin and others.

years.h: Her LP demos reach Kode9 at Hyperdub
years.p: Steve Goodman, who records as [[Kode9|e95a9d7f-fc26-4e56-8032-90cd954deea0]] and runs the label, responds positively. Quarantine follows.

eras.title: Hyperdub, and a voice nobody tuned
eras.text: Hyperdub released Quarantine in 2012 and Chance of Rain in 2013. The first has her singing with no processing on the voice; the second drops the vocals for jazz-inflected techno and musique concrete.

years.cap: Halo at a keyboard on stage
years.src: Wikipedia: Quarantine (Laurel Halo album) · Wikipedia: Laurel Halo
years.h: Hyperdub issues Quarantine with the vocals uncorrected
years.p: She recorded it at home in Brooklyn between July 2011 and February 2012, with some instruments added in London. She made more than thirty demos and threw out eighteen.
years.xp:
Halo chose not to process her voice. Per Wikipedia she said there is a "brutal, sensual ugliness in the vocals uncorrected" and that painfully human vocals made sense. She described the themes as contrails, trauma, volatile chemicals and viruses.

The cover adapts Makoto Aida's Harakiri School Girls, which she saw at a Japanese pop art show in New York. The Wire named it its release of the year, and Metacritic has an 80 for it. Tiny Mix Tapes later put it 25th among the decade's best albums.

years.h: Halo relocates to Berlin
years.p: Wikipedia dates the move from New York to 2013. She has since split her time between Berlin and Los Angeles.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chance of Rain (Laurel Halo album)
years.h: Chance of Rain goes out without a single vocal
years.p: Nine instrumentals, all produced by Halo, in a sleeve drawn by her father, Arthur Chartow, in the 1970s.
years.xp:
Wikipedia collects the reviews: Metacritic 78, Exclaim! 9/10, Pitchfork 7.4, NME 7. Fact ranked it No. 36 of 2013 and Tiny Mix Tapes placed it 14th.

It is the record where jazz-inflected techno and musique concrete take over from the singing.

eras.title: A hologram pop star, and back to Hyperdub
eras.text: After Chance of Rain she put out In Situ on Honest Jon's, scored a show for Hatsune Miku, and returned to Hyperdub with Dust. Then came a film score and the record that grew out of it.

years.h: Honest Jon's releases In Situ, a double EP
years.p: Eight instrumentals in 35 minutes. Resident Advisor praised its live-manipulated textures, and Metacritic has it at 73.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · Wikipedia: Atlas (Laurel Halo album)
years.h: Halo makes Terepa with Julia Holter and Rashad Becker
years.p: The EP on Other People also features NH'Koxyen. Becker later masters Atlas.

years.h: Hatsune Miku gets a Halo soundtrack in Berlin
years.p: CTM and Transmediale commission Still Be Here, a show built around the Vocaloid star. It premieres at HKW.

years.cap: Halo at her table, Open Source Festival, Düsseldorf
years.h: Dust begins with a two-week residency in Troy
years.p: Recording starts at EMPAC in Troy, New York, in 2015. Eli Keszler, [[Julia Holter|45610c1f-41a4-44f1-9da6-227510073ffc]], Michael Salu, Klein and Lafawndah play or sing on the Hyperdub album.
years.xp:
Halo took lyrics from concrete poetry, Aram Saroyan and Anne Carson's Sappho translations, then randomized the lines. The lead single, "Jelly," came out April 20, 2017, with vocals by Klein and Lafawndah.

Metacritic has an 84 from 18 reviews. Fact ranked it No. 6 on its 2017 list and Gorilla vs. Bear put it at No. 5.

years.h: Scoring Possessed turns into Raw Silk Uncut Wood
years.p: Six ambient pieces with [[Oliver Coates|c464a09c-6e10-469b-82a1-0234b189790c]] and Keszler, out July 13 on Latency. The title comes from Ursula Le Guin's Tao Te Ching.
years.xp: It was announced June 13, 2018 alongside the title track. Pitchfork's Sasha Geffen wrote that it marks a departure from her usual thorny, cerebral electronic compositions. Metacritic has an 84.

years.h: Halo and Hodge release Tru / Opal / The Light Within You
years.p: A collaborative EP on Livity Sound.

eras.title: Four years of runways and radio
eras.text: Between records Halo scored fashion shows, mixed a DJ-Kicks and started Awe, a radio show on NTS that became her label.

years.h: Halo scores Eckhaus Latta's Fall 2019 show
years.p: New York Fashion Week, and the first of several fashion commissions.

yt: Boiler Room New York DJ set, 2017
years.h: Her DJ-Kicks mix for !K7 is Vol. 68
years.p: It follows her first Boiler Room set, in New York in 2017.

years.h: The Possessed score comes out on the Vinyl Factory
years.p: The soundtrack for the Metahaven and Rob Schroder documentary gets its own release.

years.h: Halo walks the Chloe runway in Paris
years.p: Chloe's Spring 2021 show, at Paris Fashion Week.

years.src: Wikipedia: Laurel Halo · The FADER: Laurel Halo creates
years.h: Awe starts as a monthly NTS show
years.p: Kode9 and Mica Levi are among the guests. The name later goes on her label.
years.xp: The FADER says Atlas is the debut on her own imprint Awe, which is named for her regular NTS radio show.

years.src: The Quietus: Laurel Halo Unveils · Wikipedia: Atlas (Laurel Halo album)
years.h: A residency at Ina-GRM in Paris yields the piano sketches
years.p: She works on them at the electroacoustic institute, and they become Atlas. "Belleville" is recorded in one take in spring 2021.

years.h: Octavia premieres at Maison de la Radio
years.p: Ina-GRM commissions the multichannel work for piano and electronics. It comes out in 2024.

eras.title: Atlas
eras.text: She started teaching at CalArts, moved to Los Angeles and released the first record on her own label.

years.h: Halo joins the faculty at CalArts
years.p: She teaches in the Composition and Experimental Sound Practices program, and moves to Los Angeles that year.

years.src: Stereogum: Laurel Halo, Belleville · The Quietus: Laurel Halo Unveils · Ableton: Laurel Halo
years.h: "Belleville" arrives first, with Coby Sey singing
years.p: The lead single is piano and vibraphone, with Sey's vocals.
years.xp: Halo told Ableton the piano is "a close mic'd, one-take, softly played piano performance" with its small details blown up through compression and saturation.

q: Tracks are never done, you just let them be.
years.src: Wikipedia: Atlas (Laurel Halo album) · Ableton: Laurel Halo · Wikipedia: Laurel Halo
years.h: Pitchfork gives Atlas 8.1 and ranks it No. 26 of 2023
years.p: Bendik Giske plays sax, Lucy Railton cello and James Underwood violin across ten tracks and 40 minutes. It is the first release on her own label, Awe.
years.xp:
Piano sketches from Ina-GRM in 2021 were built out in Berlin and London with electronics and acoustic layers. Some collaborators recorded in the room, others sent parts remotely; James Ginzburg mixed and Rashad Becker mastered.

Halo told Ableton: "I'm still a hard amateur with the piano and will be in the foothills for a long time."

Metacritic has an 80. Pitchfork's review (8.1) called it among her best. Clash gave it 9/10 and ranked it No. 15 of its year. Boomkat named it its album of the year.

years.src: The Quietus: Laurel Halo Unveils · The FADER: Laurel Halo creates
yt: DJ set at HOR Berlin, Aug 21, 2023
years.h: Atlas goes live at Berlin Atonal
years.p: Dates follow in Dublin, London, Amsterdam, Bochum and Philadelphia.

eras.title: Octavia on record, then a film score
eras.text: She kept writing for spaces and screens rather than going back to songs.

years.h: GRM releases Octavia as half of a split
years.p: It comes out on Portraits GRM, paired with Jessica Ekomane's Manifolds.

years.h: A Midnight Zone soundtrack appears on her site
years.p: She lists it as an original film score.
